analysis.title: GS US TMT quick hits
key_insights: About 70% of S&P 500 constituents rose on 11/24, yet the NDX closed down about 200 bps as Semis fell 8%. The roughly 600 bps Semis underperformance vs NDX ranks among the worst 1-day lags in recent history.
Optimism around a positioning-led year-end rally faded. Frustration persists around high single-stock volatility and AI vs the rest rotations despite risk-off flows for weeks.

Desk read is that yesterday's activity was more net exposure management (macro product trading) than investing, with the single stock desk quiet. Bears cite unresolved AI supply chain questions (China, shell/permitting, ROIs, token trajectory).

Bears argue the market will struggle to rally much above pre-Election levels, let alone back to the 200-dma, on price and positioning alone. Conviction is subdued and investors are in wait-and-see mode.
Several names fell more than 15% on solid earnings (HPE, DY, ADI), which the desk reads as the market implying cuts in those areas.

ADI fell about 17% (worst day since May 1998) on softer F1Q margin and EPS guidance and guidance for higher FY27 capex. Management said about 67% of growth comes from non-AI-centric markets. GS stays Buy and EPS ests rose about 4% post print.
ADI forward P/E is now about 18x, only cheaper heading into the 18/19 and 22/23 down-cycles. ADI had outperformed the SOX by about 20 pts in C4Q into today.
Post-close earnings moves: DELL +5% on FY EPS guide raised 16% and AI server beat, NTNX -6% on earnings and CEO succession, WDAY -4%, ADSK -4% despite FY raise, HPQ -3%.
Other movers on inbounds: CPNG +9%, EBAY -4%, SWKS +8% with AAPL and QCOM also up, and a SaaS bounce questioned as squeeze or rotation.
